ai.literal: Wisdom ruin protecting tool, to enemies even inside destroying impossible fortress.
ai.translation: Wisdom is a tool that protects against ruin; it is an inner fortress that even enemies cannot destroy.
ai.modern: அறிவு என்பது ஒருவருக்கு அழிவு வராமல் காக்கும் கருவியாகும். மேலும் அது பகைவர்களாலும் அழிக்க முடியாத உள்ளரண் ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the dual protective nature of wisdom. The word 'aṟivu' (wisdom) is first described as an active tool ('karuvi') that wards off ruin or vulnerability ('aṟṟam'). Second, it is compared to a fortress ('araṇ') built within ('uḷ'). This inner defense is so strong that even determined enemies ('ceṟuvār') find it impossible to breach and destroy.

ai.literal: that goes - in the direction - to go - not letting - evil - having shunned - towards the good - directing - [is] wisdom
ai.translation: Wisdom is not letting the mind wander wherever it goes, but keeping it away from evil and directing it towards the good.
ai.modern: மனம் சென்ற திசையிலெல்லாம் அதனைச் செல்ல விடாமல் தடுத்து, தீமையானவற்றிலிருந்து விலக்கி, நன்மையான வழியில் செலுத்துவதே அறிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines true wisdom as the mastery over one's own mind. The mind naturally tends to wander wherever its desires lead it. Wisdom consists of not letting it go ('செல விடா') in those arbitrary directions. Instead, one must actively shun evil paths ('தீது ஒரீஇ') and consciously direct the mind toward what is good ('நன்றின்பால் உய்ப்பது').

ai.literal: Whatever matter, who who mouth even if heard, that matter's true nature seeing is wisdom.
ai.translation: Whatever you may hear, and from whomever's mouth you hear it, wisdom is seeing the truth in it.
ai.modern: எந்த ஒரு செய்தியை யார் யாரிடமிருந்து கேட்டாலும், அந்தச் செய்தியின் உண்மையான பொருளை ஆராய்ந்து அறிவதே அறிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines true wisdom as the ability to discern the truth objectively. The repeated word 'யார் யார்' (whoever) paired with 'வாய்' (mouth) emphasizes that the source of the information—whether a person of high status, a friend, or a stranger—should not cloud one's judgment. 'மெய்ப்பொருள்' refers to the actual truth or reality of the matter. Therefore, a wise person does not blindly accept what is said based on who says it, but critically examines the matter to find its true nature.

ai.literal: Easy meaning to become, to reach having spoken, oneself (from) others' mouths subtle meaning perceiving (is) knowledge.
ai.translation: True knowledge is speaking so clearly that one's meaning easily reaches others, and perceiving the subtle meaning in what others say.
ai.modern: தான் சொல்லும் கருத்துக்களை மற்றவர்களுக்கு எளிதில் விளங்குமாறு சொல்லி, மற்றவர்கள் சொல்லும் சொற்களில் உள்ள நுட்பமான கருத்துக்களை ஆராய்ந்து அறிவதே உண்மையான அறிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines what constitutes true intellectual communication and comprehension. The first half focuses on expression: 'எண்பொருள ஆகச் செலச் சொல்லி' means speaking in a way that makes complex ideas easy to grasp and readily reach the listener's mind. The second half focuses on reception: 'பிறர்வாய் நுண்பொருள் காண்பது' means extracting the subtle, deep meaning from the words of others, regardless of how they express it. Together, these two skills—simplifying one's own thoughts for others and penetrating the surface of others' words to find the core truth—embody true knowledge.

ai.literal: The world that which embraces [is] wisdom; blooming and closing that which is without [is] knowledge.
ai.translation: Wisdom is that which embraces the world. True knowledge is that which neither blooms nor closes.
ai.modern: உலகத்தாரோடு பொருந்தி வாழ்வதே சிறந்த மதிநுட்பமாகும். மகிழ்ச்சியால் விரிவதும் துன்பத்தால் சுருங்குவதும் இல்லாத மனநிலையே உண்மையான அறிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines two aspects of the intellect: practical wisdom and true knowledge. Wisdom (ஒட்பம்) is the ability to embrace the world, meaning to adapt and live in harmony with others. Knowledge (அறிவு) is described through the metaphor of a flower that neither blooms nor closes. This signifies a state of equanimity, where the mind neither expands with pride and joy nor shrinks with fear and sorrow.

ai.translation: Wisdom is to live in harmony with the world, conducting oneself in whatever way the world conducts itself.
ai.modern: உலகம் எப்படி வாழ்கிறதோ, அந்த உலகத்தோடு பொருந்தி அதே வழியில் வாழ்வதே அறிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines practical wisdom as adaptability and social harmony. The word 'உறைவது' means dwelling or living, indicating one's conduct in daily life. True wisdom is not just theoretical knowledge, but the ability to understand the ways of the world and live in accordance with them.

ai.literal: Those who possess wisdom will know what will happen; those without wisdom are those who cannot know that.
ai.translation: The wise foresee what is to come. The unwise are those who cannot foresee it.
ai.modern: அறிவுடையவர்கள் எதிர்காலத்தில் நடக்கப்போவதை முன்கூட்டியே அறிவார்கள். அறிவில்லாதவர்கள் அதனை அறிய முடியாதவர்கள் ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines wisdom as the capacity for foresight. The word 'ஆவது' refers to what will happen in the future or the natural consequences of one's actions. The wise ('அறிவுடையார்') are able to anticipate these outcomes and act accordingly. In contrast, those lacking wisdom ('அறிவிலார்') are characterized precisely by their inability ('அறிகல்லாதவர்') to foresee what is to come.

ai.literal: That which is to be feared not fearing is folly; that which is to be feared fearing is those who know's action.
ai.translation: It is folly not to fear what ought to be feared. Fearing what should be feared is the action of the wise.
ai.modern: அஞ்ச வேண்டியவற்றுக்கு அஞ்சாமல் இருப்பது அறியாமையாகும். அஞ்ச வேண்டியவற்றுக்கு அஞ்சுவதே அறிவுடையவர்களின் செயலாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the relationship between fear and wisdom. The word 'அஞ்சுவது' refers to things that naturally warrant caution, such as doing wrong or facing real danger. 'அஞ்சாமை' (not fearing) in such situations is not bravery, but 'பேதைமை' (foolishness). Conversely, 'அஞ்சல்' (fearing) what should be feared is the proper 'தொழில்' (action or duty) of 'அறிவார்' (those who possess knowledge). True wisdom involves recognizing risks and responding with appropriate caution.

ai.literal: Guarding against the future, to the wise there is not a pain that comes to make them tremble.
ai.translation: Those with the wisdom to foresee and guard against the future will suffer no terrifying afflictions.
ai.modern: எதிர்காலத்தில் வரப்போவதை முன்னே அறிந்து காத்துக்கொள்ளும் அறிவுடையவர்களுக்கு, அவர்கள் நடுங்கும்படியாக வரும் துன்பம் எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the protective power of foresight. The phrase 'எதிரதாக் காக்கும்' refers to anticipating future events and taking preventive measures. Because the wise prepare in advance, no sudden or overwhelming disaster can catch them off guard and cause them to tremble.

ai.literal: Those who possess knowledge everything they possess; those without knowledge whatever they possess even if, they are without.
ai.translation: Those who possess wisdom possess everything. Those without wisdom possess nothing, no matter what else they may have.
ai.modern: அறிவுடையவர்கள் உலகத்தில் உள்ள எல்லாவற்றையும் பெற்றவர்கள் ஆவார்கள். அறிவு இல்லாதவர்கள் வேறு எதைப் பெற்றிருந்தாலும், உண்மையில் ஒன்றும் இல்லாதவர்களே ஆவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the true value of wisdom with material possessions. The word 'அறிவுடையார்' refers to those who have acquired true knowledge, and the poet declares that they effectively possess everything. Conversely, 'அறிவிலார்' are those lacking wisdom; even if they own vast wealth or other worldly goods ('என் உடையரேனும்'), they are considered to have nothing ('இலர்'). The underlying message is that knowledge is the only complete and secure possession, rendering all other acquisitions meaningless without it.
